blocks.text: # Proofpress continuous-canvas motion system

This instruction captures the reusable visual grammar behind the Proofpress
launch film. Use it with the HyperFrames core, creative, animation, and CLI
skills when extending this film or building a new Proofpress motion piece. It is
a brand-specific layer on top of those skills, not a replacement for their
composition and determinism rules.
## Core idea

Treat the whole film as one explorable knowledge space. Stations live on a
single oversized canvas and the camera follows one continuous route through
them. The artifact is the stable subject; sessions, ledgers, and claims are
places the camera visits around it. A transition should reveal a causal
relationship, not announce that a new slide has begun.
## Visual registers
- Barlow Condensed is the declarative voice: category claims, causal statements,
station titles, and closing language.
- IBM Plex Mono is the evidentiary voice: session labels, versions, metadata,
ledger qualifiers, and URLs.
- Newsreader is an occasional reflective voice. Do not switch into it inside a
short causal statement merely to create variety.
- Warm paper represents the artifact. Teal represents the live Proofpress route

and admitted ledger. Gold represents stated reasoning. Muted red represents a
  rejected direction. Green is reserved for a computed check.

Do not introduce a fourth typographic voice, gradient type, rounded SaaS cards,
security shields, identity chrome, floating particles, or ambient motion that
is unrelated to the artifact's lineage.
## Camera grammar

1. Build stations at fixed coordinates on one world canvas.
2. Move the world with one seek-safe camera object and a single paused GSAP
timeline. Use translation and scale only.
3. Let incoming words land while the camera decelerates so the world feels
continuous.
4. A zoom must resolve into meaning. After reaching a readable close-up, hold
for 0.5–0.8 seconds before leaving or reveal the next layer inside the object.
5. Match direction across handoffs: an accelerating exit meets a decelerating
entry. Avoid a zoom that ends on the same frame as an unrelated camera move.
6. The artifact may travel, fold, or scale, but it must remain recognizably the
same object across the sequence.
## Rhythm

Use the pattern `DECLARE → TRAVEL → HOLD → OPEN → PROVE → TRAVEL → HOLD`.
Statements arrive quickly; evidence receives longer reading time. The first
two seconds establish the category. The handoff gets one complete visual
sentence. The document close-up gets a perceptible hold. Ledger rows reveal in
the order `EDIT → WHY → REJECTED`, followed by the distinction `REASON STATED /
CHANGE CHECKED`. The open-source close stays fully stable for at least 2.5
seconds.
## Feed-scale typography

Design for the video as it appears inside the X feed, not for a full-screen
desktop preview. In 1920×1080, use 90px or larger for essential headlines,
32px or larger for explanatory copy, and 24px or larger for essential labels.
Tiny mono text may exist only as nonessential texture. The square version must
reflow the same hierarchy rather than crop the widescreen composition.
## Semantic rules
- Show a real document change, a stated reason, and a consequential rejected
direction that belong to the same fictional strategy artifact.

- Visually separate computed/checkable changes from attributed context.
- Never imply signed identity, authorization, policy enforcement, or complete
capture of a private conversation.
- The ledger travels with the artifact; the source session does not need to
travel with it.
## Reuse prompt

> Use the Proofpress continuous-canvas motion system in `MOTION_SYSTEM.md`.
> Preserve the dark editorial field, paper artifact, teal lineage route, three
> typographic registers, semantic color roles, and one-world camera grammar.
> Build all motion on one paused, seek-safe HyperFrames timeline. For every
> camera move, name the idea it reveals and include a readable hold after any
> close-up. Keep the artifact continuous, make evidence legible at X feed size,
> and distinguish stated context from computed checks. Reflow separately for
> square; do not crop the 16:9 composition.
## Review checklist

- Can a silent viewer explain why the camera moved at every transition?
- Does every zoom include enough time to recognize what was enlarged?
- Are all essential words readable in a phone-sized X preview?
- Does each font correspond to a stable communicative role?
- Does the artifact preserve identity through the entire handoff?
- Are `EDIT`, `WHY`, `REJECTED`, and computed verification visually distinct?
- Does a seek to any point reproduce the same frame without wall-clock state?
